tasks.short: Review the chart, X-rays and medical history, examine and diagnose, treat teeth and gums, and record findings and treatment.

steps.what: Dentist reviews the chart, X-rays and medical history before treatment
Dentist examines teeth and gums and diagnoses diseases, injuries or malformations
Dentist treats teeth, gums or related oral structures and provides preventive services
Dentist dictates findings and treatment for the assistant to type

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the charted items.
loop.output: A draft treatment note in the practice template.
loop.check: Treatment codes come from the charted items, not the model; the dentist reads and validates every note before it is saved.
loop.stop: No unvalidated note is saved; without consent the dentist dictates as before.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken findings vary; a fixed template cannot turn speech into a note.

tasks.design: The dental record ({OTHER}) shows chart, X-rays, medication and medical history on one screen. With the patient's consent, a certified scribe drafts the treatment note from the consultation and the charted items; the dentist validates every note before it is saved. Examining, diagnosing and treating stay with the dentist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were dictated to the assistant and typed afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified ambient scribes draft notes for validation inside the record.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can miss or misstate findings, so every note needs reading.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling a cavity under a filling that the X-ray does not show.

reach.learn: Whether the assistant's typing time disappears.

evidence.claim: At Capio, across 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; median editing stayed 93 seconds.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, train, test and monitor after updates.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient record to the treatment note; billing is outside.
Input contract: charted items by the dentist; recording only with patient consent; fallback is dictation.
Examining and treating do not change.
The assistant's typing time is outside the dentist's savings.
research_questions: How long does the dentist spend validating each note?

incremental.description: Dentist asks patients for consent to record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients decline recording; high: most consent and notes need light edits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check rosters and leave, supervise and coach staff, sign paperwork, check insurance claims, submit them, and interview and hire staff.

steps.what: Dentist checks staff rosters and leave requests
Dentist supervises and coaches the practice staff
Dentist handles paperwork such as supplier orders and contracts
Dentist checks insurance claims before they go
Dentist submits insurance claims to insurers
Dentist interviews and employs new staff

tasks.design: Leave requests and rosters move to a scheduling tool ({HCM}) with the practice's opening hours, so the dentist approves rather than builds the roster. Claims are built from the charted treatment codes in the practice system ({OTHER}), which flags codes insurers often reject; once the dentist has checked the list, claims go to insurers electronically. Supervising, coaching and hiring stay with the dentist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters lived in spreadsheets and claims were checked line by line.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems build claims from treatment codes and send them electronically.
tasks.still_hard: Staff shortages make rosters a negotiation, not a calculation.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a small team working well together on busy days.
tasks.altitude: The dentist checks flagged claims instead of every line.

evidence.claim: Dental practice systems build insurance claims from treatment codes and send them electronically.
Health data in claims are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from leave requests and treatment codes to submitted claims and new staff; payroll is outside.
Input contract: treatment codes charted by dentists; leave requests from staff in the scheduling tool; fallback is spreadsheets.
Supervising and hiring do not change.
Staff enter leave requests in the tool instead of on paper; about the same time.

incremental.description: Dentist keeps opening hours and roster rules current.

approvals.approved_version: The claims as checked by the dentist in s4; corrected claims need a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a practice with a practice manager who already checks claims; high: a solo practice where the dentist does it all.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review each patient's charting and X-ray history, compare caries and gum scores with earlier visits, evaluate dental needs and risk, and look at practice-wide disease patterns.

steps.what: Dentist reviews each patient's charting and X-ray history at check-ups
Dentist compares caries and gum scores with earlier visits
Dentist evaluates dental needs to determine changes in patterns of dental disease for each patient
Dentist looks at practice-wide trends in dental disease once a year

tasks.design: The dental record ({OTHER}) charts caries and gum scores over time per patient, so changes since earlier visits show as a graph instead of being compared by hand. A practice dashboard shows disease patterns by age group and risk class. Evaluating each patient's needs stays with the dentist; no software makes the diagnosis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier charts were opened one by one and compared by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Dental records chart scores over time and feed practice dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Scores recorded differently by different dentists do not compare well.
tasks.human_edge: Linking a new pattern of decay to a change in the patient's life.

ambition.what: Review practice-wide disease patterns every quarter instead of yearly.

tasks.altitude: The dentist reads trends instead of building them.

reach.learn: Whether score trends change recall intervals.

evidence.claim: Dental record systems chart caries and periodontal scores over time.
The medical dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the dental record to practice trends; treatment planning is outside.
Input contract: scores charted by dentists and hygienists in agreed units; fallback is comparing charts by eye.
Dashboards show groups, not named patients.
research_questions: Do recall intervals follow risk more closely?

already_counted.description: Dentist reads score graphs at check-ups.

incremental.description: Dentist agrees scoring rules with colleagues.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: scores recorded inconsistently across dentists; high: all dentists chart in the same units.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check the medication list and allergies, choose the drug and dose, write the prescription, resolve interaction alerts, send it to the pharmacy and explain use to the patient.

steps.what: Dentist checks the patient's medication list and allergies
Dentist chooses the antibiotic or other medication and the dose
Dentist writes prescriptions by hand or types them
Dentist resolves interaction and allergy alerts and signs the prescription
Dentist sends the prescription to the patient's pharmacy
Dentist explains how to take the medication to the patient

tasks.design: The dental record ({OTHER}) imports the patient's medication overview and allergies, and the prescribing module runs rule-based checks for interactions, contraindications and doses. Prescriptions start from a dental formulary with standard doses. The dentist chooses, resolves alerts and signs, and only then does the e-prescription go to the pharmacy. Choosing and explaining stay with the dentist; no model prescribes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication lists were asked from patients, and prescriptions handwritten or typed in full.
tasks.enabler_now: Prescribing modules check interactions against national drug content and send e-prescriptions.
tasks.still_hard: Patients' medication overviews are not always complete.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding an antibiotic is not needed at all.

reach.learn: Whether e-prescriptions cut queries to the practice.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates, with content set by the KNMP.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software may draft but not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient record to the instructed patient; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: medication overview with the patient's consent; formulary kept by the practice; fallback is asking the patient and writing by hand.
Choosing, resolving alerts and explaining stay with the dentist.
Pharmacists' time is outside the dentist's savings.
research_questions: Do interaction problems reported by pharmacies fall?

incremental.description: Dentist keeps the dental formulary current.

approvals.approved_version: The prescription as signed by the dentist in s4; a change needs a new signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients without a medication overview on file; high: most overviews available.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The dentist keeps diagnosing, treating, prescribing decisions and leading the team; typed notes, line-by-line claims, comparing charts and handwritten prescriptions shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A dentist who spends saved minutes explaining care to patients.
